mainTopic: How a קנין affects a deathbed gift (מתנת שכיב מרע), and what happens when a שכיב מרע gives the same property to two people one after the other
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ruling that רבא found difficult: when a שכיב מרע makes a קנין, it is clear he did it only because he expected to die. רב נחמן answers with a silent hand gesture, and רבא later explains it to רב נחמן בר יצחק. The case is one where the giver was strengthening the recipient's position (מיפה את כחו). רב חסדא defines that case by the wording of the document: 'and we acquired from him in addition to this gift.' The גמרא then turns to a שכיב מרע who gives the same property to two people. If he only wrote documents, the later one cancels the earlier, as רב דימי taught. If he also transferred possession each time, רב says the first recipient wins because it is like a healthy person's gift, and שמואל says the second wins because it is still a deathbed gift. The גמרא explains why this dispute is needed alongside their earlier dispute about a deathbed gift with a written קנין. Finally it brings the פומבדיתא version, where רב's study hall sends שמואל a question and he replies 'after a קנין there is nothing.' The next amud discusses what that reply means.

steps.title: The end of the ruling that raised the difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ruling ends with its reason: it is known that the קנין was done only because the giver expected to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is known that the act of acquisition was done only because of the expected death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ruling that רבא found difficult. Its reason is that the קנין was clearly done only because the giver thought he was dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קנין looks like the giver wants the gift to work like a healthy person's gift. This ruling says no: a dying man's קנין is just part of his deathbed gift. That clashes with another ruling that treats the קנין as meaningful, and that clash is the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: it is known, it is clear

phrases.english: It is known that the act of acquisition was not
except because of the expected death.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה קִנְיָן אֶלָּא מֵחֲמַת הַמִּיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source that רבא raised as a contradiction before this point
steps.kashyaTarget: The other ruling, which seems to treat a קנין in a deathbed gift as meaningful
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ruling says a dying man's קנין is only because of death and changes nothing, which seems to contradict that other ruling

steps.title: רב נחמן answers with a hand gesture
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא silently with a hand gesture, and רבא accepts it and is quiet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He showed him with his hand, and he was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the difficulty without words, using a hand gesture. רבא understands and stays quiet, which shows he accepted the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not spelled out yet. The גמרא is setting up the next steps, where רבא explains what the gesture meant.

phrases.english: And he showed him with his hand,
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is the one gesturing, and he is gesturing to רבא.

phrases.english: and he (רבא) was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from step 1, but without words
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unspoken answer, explained later in step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: There is an answer; רבא accepts it by staying silent

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks what the gesture meant
steps.stepSummary: After רב נחמן leaves, רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא what the gesture meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he got up, רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: What did he show you?
steps.whatsHappening: Once רב נחמן gets up, a different scholar asks רבא to explain the silent answer. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different people are named נחמן here. רב נחמן gave the gesture. רב נחמן בר יצחק is the student asking about it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב נחמן (who gestured) with רב נחמן בר יצחק (who asks what it meant). They are two different people.

phrases.english: When he got up,
phrases.notes: This means רב נחמן got up and left.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rava:
What did he show you?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָם, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא: מַאי אַחְוִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the silent answer in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What answer the hand gesture was giving

steps.title: The gesture meant: the giver was strengthening the recipient
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the gesture meant the case is one where the giver was strengthening the recipient's power (מיפה את כחו).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is talking about one who strengthens his power.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the gesture. The ruling refers to a giver who added the קנין only to make the recipient's position stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the קנין is an extra layer of strength on top of the gift. It does not show that the giver meant to make a healthy person's gift. This resolves the contradiction from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: strengthens his power, makes the recipient's position stronger

steps.whyThisMatters: A קנין does not always mean the same thing. Its meaning depends on why it was added.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is about one who strengthens his power.
phrases.notes: The giver is strengthening the power of the person receiving the gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and spells out the answer to step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one where the קנין was added only to strengthen the recipient, not to change the kind of gift

steps.title: What counts as strengthening the recipient?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case counts as 'strengthening his power'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of one who strengthens his power?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of מיפה את כחו. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea from step 4 is still general. The גמרא wants a clear sign that shows us when a קנין was added only for strength.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case, what does it look like

phrases.english: What is the case of one who strengthens his power?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete sign that a קנין was done only to strengthen the gift

steps.title: רב חסדא: the document says the קנין is in addition to the gift
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says it is when the document reads: 'and we acquired from him in addition to this gift.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: When it is written, 'And we acquired from him, in addition to this gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the wording that shows the giver was only strengthening the recipient. The document says the קנין was added on top of the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'in addition' shows that the gift itself works as a deathbed gift. The קנין is just extra support, not what makes the gift take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: and we (the witnesses) acquired from him

steps.whatToRemember: A קנין in a deathbed gift can be just 'extra strength'. When the document says it is added on top of the gift (מוסיף על מתנתא דא), it does not turn the deathbed gift into a healthy person's gift.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
"And we acquired from him
phrases.notes: This is the wording written in the document. The 'we' are the witnesses.

phrases.english: in addition to this gift."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וּקְנֵינָא מִינֵּיהּ מוֹסִיף עַל מַתַּנְתָּא דָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the document says the קנין was 'in addition to this gift'

steps.title: Two documents to two people: the later one cancels the earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that if a שכיב מרע wrote the property to one person and then to another, this is רב דימי's rule: a later will cancels an earlier will.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he wrote to this one and wrote to that one, this is what רב דימי said when he came: A later will cancels an earlier will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a שכיב מרע who gives the same property to two people in writing. Since he only wrote documents, the later one wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed gift works like a will, and a person can change his will until he dies. So the second document cancels the first. This simple case sets up the harder case in the next step.

phrases.english: It is obvious:
if he wrote to this one and wrote to that one,
phrases.notes: He gave the same property, first to one person and then to another.

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: this is what Rav Dimi said when he came:
phrases.notes: רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: A will cancels a will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about two deathbed gifts of the same property
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there are only documents, the later deathbed document cancels the earlier one

steps.title: Wrote and transferred to two people: רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: If he wrote and also transferred possession to one person, then did the same to another, רב says the first gets it and שמואל says the second gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote and transferred possession to this one, then wrote and transferred possession to that one: רב says the first acquired it, and שמואל says the second acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the harder case, where each gift came with an actual transfer of possession, not just a document. רב and שמואל disagree about who gets the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the gift came with a real transfer (זיכה), so it is less clear that it can be changed like a will. רב says the first transfer holds. שמואל says the later one still wins.

keyTerms.meaning: and he transferred possession, gave him ownership

steps.whyThisMatters: This disagreement is the starting point for the discussion that follows about how a transfer of possession affects a deathbed gift.

phrases.english: If he wrote and transferred possession to this one,
and then wrote and transferred possession to that one:
Rav says: The first acquired it,
and Shmuel says: The second acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב וְזִיכָּה לָזֶה, כָּתַב וְזִיכָּה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious case in step 7 to a harder case that is disputed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the first recipient acquires. שמואל: the second recipient acquires.

steps.title: The reasons behind the views of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב says the first recipient acquires because the gift is like a healthy person's gift. שמואל says the second acquires because it is still a deathbed gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: the first one acquires, because it is like a gift of a healthy person. שמואל says: the second one acquires, because it is like a gift of a שכיב מרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two opinions in the case from the last step and attaches a reason to each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the שכיב מרע 'wrote and transferred', רב treats the gift as a full, regular gift, like one from a healthy person, and that kind of gift cannot be taken back. שמואל says it is still a deathbed gift, so the later gift cancels the earlier one, just like a later will cancels an earlier will.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift from a healthy person. It becomes final and cannot be taken back.
A gift from a person on his deathbed. It works like a will and can be changed.

steps.whyThisMatters: Everything in the rest of this section depends on this question: does an act of transfer turn a deathbed gift into a final, healthy person's gift?

phrases.english: Rav says: the first one acquires –
it is like the gift of a healthy person.
And Shmuel says: the second one acquires –
it is like the gift of a person on his deathbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the dispute presented in step 8 by giving each side's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the gift is like a healthy person's gift, so the first recipient keeps it. שמואל: it is still a deathbed gift, so the second recipient gets it.

steps.title: Haven't רב and שמואל already argued about this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this dispute is needed, since רב and שמואל already argued about a deathbed gift whose document mentions a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once, in the case of a deathbed gift in which a קנין is written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for this dispute, because it seems to repeat an argument רב and שמואל already had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier dispute, רב held that a קנין makes the deathbed gift final, and שמואל held that it does not. That looks like the very same question as here, so recording both disputes seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A formal act that transfers ownership.

phrases.english: But they already argued about this once –

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ קִנְיָן!
phrases.english: about a gift of a person on his deathbed in which a kinyan is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the dispute in steps 8-9 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to record the dispute of רב and שמואל in this case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same principle was already argued in the case of a deathbed gift with a written קנין, so this second dispute seems repetitive.

steps.title: Both disputes are needed
steps.stepSummary: Each case teaches something new. From the קנין case alone we might think רב agrees with שמואל here, and from this case alone we might think שמואל agrees with רב there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If they had argued only in that case, we would say רב rules that way only there, because a קנין was done, but here, with no קנין, he agrees with שמואל. And if they had argued only in this case, we would say שמואל rules that way only here, but in the other case he agrees with רב. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both disputes are needed, because each one shuts down a mistake we could have made from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנין case is the strong case for רב, since a real act of acquisition was done. So we learn that רב holds his view even without one. The case here, with no separate קנין, is the strong case for שמואל. So we learn that שמואל holds his view even when a קנין was done.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. The גמרא's way of showing that two teachings that look alike are both needed.
I might say, we would have thought.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of which 'this' is which. The first 'בהא' is the earlier case, where a קנין was written. 'בהא דלא קנו מיניה' is the case here, where no separate קנין was done. In the second half the order flips.
steps.whatToRemember: רב always holds the gift is final, with or without a קנין. שמואל always holds it can be changed, with or without a קנין.

phrases.english: It is necessary;
because if it were stated in that case –
phrases.notes: This is the earlier case, the deathbed gift where a קנין was written.

phrases.english: only in that case does Rav say so,
because they made a kinyan with him;
but in this case, where they did not make a kinyan with him –
I would say he agrees with Shmuel.
And if it were stated in this case –
phrases.notes: Now 'this' means our case, where he wrote and transferred without a separate קנין.

phrases.english: only in this case does Shmuel say so;
but in that other case –
I would say he agrees with Rav;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches a point the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could have thought רב's view depends on a real קנין, and שמואל's view applies only when there is no קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one holds his position in both cases, so both disputes are recorded.

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version: a question sent to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: In סורא they taught the dispute as above. In פומבדיתא they taught that רב's study hall asked שמואל about a deathbed gift of all one's property done with a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it this way. In פומבדיתא they taught it this way: רב ירמיה בר אבא said, they sent from the study hall of רב to שמואל: 'Let our teacher teach us: a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to others, and they made a קנין with him, what is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the teaching, from פומבדיתא. It sets up a question that was sent to שמואל, and his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the teaching is not given as a dispute between רב and שמואל. Instead, רב's study hall sends שמואל a question about a deathbed gift of all one's property done with a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let our teacher teach us. A respectful way to open a question.
They made a קנין with him, a formal act of acquisition.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught it this way;
phrases.notes: This means the version we just learned, with רב and שמואל arguing.

phrases.english: in Pumbedita they taught it this way,
Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
they sent from the study hall of Rav to Shmuel,
Let our teacher teach us:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתַב כׇּל נְכָסָיו לַאֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: a person on his deathbed who wrote all his property to others,
and they made a kinyan with him, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי; בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a different version of the teaching from steps 8-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קנין make a deathbed gift of all one's property final, so that it cannot be taken back?

steps.title: שמואל: after a קנין, nothing can undo it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that once a קנין has been done, nothing can cancel the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to them: after a קנין, there is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: once a קנין was done, the gift is final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its face, שמואל's short reply says that once a קנין was done, nothing can take the gift back. This sounds very different from his position in the סורא version. The amud ends here, and the גמרא keeps discussing what this reply means on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: After a קנין there is nothing, meaning nothing can cancel the gift.

steps.whatToRemember: In סורא, רב and שמואל argue. In פומבדיתא, the teaching is a question sent to שמואל, and his reply is 'after a קנין there is nothing.' The next amud discusses what that reply means.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
After a kinyan there is nothing.
phrases.notes: He means nothing can come after the קנין and take the gift back.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: אֵין אַחַר קִנְיָן כְּלוּם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A deathbed gift done with a קנין is final and cannot be undone.
